text: How to open a book, move through it, and use what is on the page.

shapes.text:
How to open a book, move through it,
and use what is on the page.
Pick a part. Next walks the book in order.

text: A Foolbook book is a file. The usual name ends in .fbk. Open it and you get pages. A page is a picture made of words, boxes, and buttons.

shapes.text:
A Foolbook book is a file. The usual name ends in .fbk. Open it and
you get pages. A page is a picture made of words, boxes, and
buttons.

This book is one of those files. It is here so the program has
something to show on a new install. First Light is the smaller one
beside it.

text: The window has three jobs. The shelf is the row of books you can open without hunting for a file. The list on the left is the pages of the book that is open. The large area is the page itself.

shapes.text:
The window has three jobs. The shelf is the row of books you can
open without hunting for a file. The list on the left is the pages
of the book that is open. The large area is the page itself.

Prev and Next sit above the page. They move one page at a time. A
button drawn on the page can jump farther than that.

text: The shelf is a convenience, not the library. First Light, Using Foolbook, and Using Grok ship with Foolbook. The tax lessons and the phone lesson come from Foolcourse.

shapes.text:
The shelf is a convenience, not the library. First Light, Using
Foolbook, and Using Grok ship with Foolbook. The tax lessons and the
phone lesson come from Foolcourse.

Clicking a name opens that book from its published file. Your own
file is not on the shelf until you use Open a book.

text: Open a book reads a file from your computer. It does not upload it anywhere. Foolbook accepts .fbk and .fsk. A ToolBook .tbk or .sbk is opened with the ToolBook reader. An .fbk that is really a ToolBook file is still read as ToolBook.

shapes.text:
Open a book reads a file from your computer. It does not upload it
anywhere. Foolbook accepts .fbk and .fsk. A ToolBook .tbk or .sbk is
opened with the ToolBook reader. An .fbk that is really a ToolBook
file is still read as ToolBook.

If the program cannot read the file, the status line under the
buttons says so. The page you had open stays put.

text: Every page has an id, such as P0 or P10. The list on the left shows that id and the first line of words on the page, so you can tell them apart.

shapes.text:
Every page has an id, such as P0 or P10. The list on the left shows
that id and the first line of words on the page, so you can tell
them apart.

The order in the list is the order of the book. Next follows that
order. A button may skip ahead. The id is the name a button uses. It
is not a page number printed for a student.

text: Next goes to the following page in the list. Back goes to the one before it. On the last page, Next stays there. On the first page, Back stays there.

shapes.text:
Next goes to the following page in the list. Back goes to the one
before it. On the last page, Next stays there. On the first page,
Back stays there.

The buttons above the page do the same job. Use those when the page
itself has no Next of its own. This book puts Next on the pages so
you can stay inside the page.

text: A button is a click that names a page. If the page is in this book, you go there. If the name is another book, Foolbook looks on the shelf. First Light, on the cover of this book, is that kind of click.

shapes.text:
A button is a click that names a page. If the page is in this book,
you go there. If the name is another book, Foolbook looks on the
shelf. First Light, on the cover of this book, is that kind of
click.

If the book is not on the shelf, the status line tells you the name.
Open that file yourself. The website viewer can also ask the page
around it, which is how Foolcourse hands over a lesson.

text: Words are a text shape. They have a place, a width, a size, and a color. A line break in the text is a new line. The box clips anything that does not fit, so a short box hides the end of a sentence.

shapes.text:
Words are a text shape. They have a place, a width, a size, and a
color. A line break in the text is a new line. The box clips
anything that does not fit, so a short box hides the end of a
sentence.

Color is the ink. On a dark header the ink is white. On the paper it
is near black. If both the ink and the fill are pale, the viewer
darkens the ink so the line can be read.

text: A picture in a Foolbook file is stored with the page and drawn in its box. A ToolBook picture is read from the file when the page opens and turned into a PNG, because a browser will not reliably draw the original bitmap.

shapes.text:
A picture in a Foolbook file is stored with the page and drawn in
its box. A ToolBook picture is read from the file when the page
opens and turned into a PNG, because a browser will not reliably
draw the original bitmap.

A button face is a picture with a click. If the face is missing, the
button is still a button: the words on it are the click.

text: A page is built from a few kinds of shape. A rect is a box. An ellipse is a round. A polygon is a run of points, used here as a roof. Text is words. A button is a rect that goes somewhere.

shapes.text:
A page is built from a few kinds of shape. A rect is a box. An
ellipse is a round. A polygon is a run of points, used here as a
roof. Text is words. A button is a rect that goes somewhere.

Nothing on this page is a photograph. It is the same drawing the
first short book used, kept so you can see the pieces.

Rect, ellipse, polygon.
The house is three of each.

text: Some clicks leave the book. The cover of this one opens First Light at its first page. Foolcourse does the same thing when you pick a lesson: it tells the viewer the address of that .fbk.

shapes.text:
Some clicks leave the book. The cover of this one opens First Light
at its first page. Foolcourse does the same thing when you pick a
lesson: it tells the viewer the address of that .fbk.

The viewer does not keep a private copy of every course. It opens
the file it was given. That is why a lesson can live in another
repository and still show up here.

text: ToolBook books end in .tbk. The matching system books end in .sbk. Foolbook reads those formats. Pages, fields, buttons, and the pictures it knows how to pull out are drawn. A click that says go to a page follows that page.

shapes.text:
ToolBook books end in .tbk. The matching system books end in .sbk.
Foolbook reads those formats. Pages, fields, buttons, and the
pictures it knows how to pull out are drawn. A click that says go to
a page follows that page.

A click that names a page in a different ToolBook file is reported,
not invented. You open the other file. The website does not store
those files.

text: Foolcourse is the shelf of a curriculum. It lists subjects, modules, and lessons. Foolbook is the window a lesson opens in. On the website, Foolcourse puts Foolbook in a frame and sends it the lesson.

shapes.text:
Foolcourse is the shelf of a curriculum. It lists subjects, modules,
and lessons. Foolbook is the window a lesson opens in. On the
website, Foolcourse puts Foolbook in a frame and sends it the
lesson.

A lesson listed with no file stays in the list and says the book is
not in the folder. That is a missing file, not a broken viewer.

text: If a picture does not load, the words and the buttons are still there. Use the words. A blank rectangle with a name is a picture the file named and the viewer could not draw.

shapes.text:
If a picture does not load, the words and the buttons are still
there. Use the words. A blank rectangle with a name is a picture the
file named and the viewer could not draw.

Buttons at the bottom of a page were added because the page named a
destination and did not draw the button itself. They are real
clicks. They are not a second copy of a button you can already see.

text: The ending tells the reader which rules to use. .tbk and .sbk are ToolBook. An .fbk that still has a ToolBook header is read as ToolBook too.

shapes.text:
The ending tells the reader which rules to use. .tbk and .sbk are
ToolBook. An .fbk that still has a ToolBook header is read as
ToolBook too.

text: ToolBook files open in the same window. Pictures the reader can pull out are drawn. A page that lives in a different file is named, and you open that file.

shapes.text:
ToolBook files open in the same window. Pictures the reader can pull
out are drawn. A page that lives in a different file is named, and
you open that file.

text: Open a file, or pick one from the shelf. Use the list when you know the page. Use Next when you do not. Click the thing that says where it goes.

shapes.text:
Open a file, or pick one from the shelf. Use the list when you know
the page. Use Next when you do not. Click the thing that says where
it goes.

If you are writing a book, the pages you just saw are the pieces: a
paper, a header, words, a few shapes, and a button with a page id.
First Light is the short version of the same idea.
